blocks.text: The stomach has a highly acidic environment with a low pH (1.5–3.5). This acidity is regulated by parietal cells, which actively pump hydrogen ions (H⁺) into the stomach. This process is important for digesting food and killing bacteria. Although the stomach has very low pH but it protects itself via a thick layer of mucus and bicarbonate ions, which neutralize acid at the cell surface. The low pH of stomach can cause non-specific reactions, meaning it can chemically change some drugs. For example, some drugs may break down in the acidic environment before they can be absorbed into the bloodstream. This is why some medications are given in a protective coating that only dissolves in the less acidic small intestine.
